Juego de lucha entretenido, barato y sencillo inspirados en los árcades de street figther 2 de los años 90, con un total de 8 luchadores cada uno con sus motivaciones y sus roles en la sociedad, con historias entrelazadas entre sí, supuestamente existe una ola de delincuencia grave que se ha liberado entre policías y terroristas en las calles de corea del sur y tienes que descubrir quien es el mentor entre las sombras de la corrupción en la ciudad de Neo Seúl.
Cada personaje tiene movimientos que se ejecutan fácilmente con patadas y golpes además de armas especiales como pistolas, bombas, ácidos o metralletas, pero la mayoría hay que recargarlas para evitar que los jugadores las spameen. Algunos combates requieren que cumplas algunos objetivos por ejemplo que ganes usando alguna arma de tu arsenal o ganar sobreviviendo al límite de tiempo, etcétera.
Al igual que otros juegos de lucha a medida que completes los modos historia y árcades puedes desbloquear y probar otros modos, por ejemplo el modo duelo que consiste básicamente en quien da el primer golpe gana, luego se desbloquea el modo turbo, una vez superado dar paso al modo experto (solo varía la dificultad, no he visto mucha diferencia).
Visualmente no desagrada a la vista, tiene esa onda de juego de sega genesis de 16 bit con colores violetas y neón, la música es aceptable y no es repetitiva, si hurgan en los archivos de steam están las pistas para escucharlas individualmente.

El juego es entretenido para pasar el rato, lamentablemente no cuenta con modo on line, solo para el combate local, viene totalmente en ingles, es compatible con Joystick en este caso usé el de Xbox S, cuesta menos de 5 dólares en steam y en oferta 2 dólares, por lo tanto es muy accesible para unas horas de entretenimiento

Considering the affordable price, I would consider this game extremely worth it as a big fighting game enjoyer myself. The main reason I decided to give it a shot is the fact that there are many aspects in this game that reminds me a lot of Street Fighter II, and that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. Once you get into the character selection screen you'll see how much it looks like Street Fighter II, even some characters moves are similar to some Street Fighter II characters, and the developers took an interesting approach on that one, I'll tell you that.

But unfortunately, the game has some issues that I think the developers could've put some more effort on:

• Combos are not optimized
-> I can't 100% guarantee that it's possible to do infinite combos in this game, but I do feel like sometimes some attacks should not CHAIN by any means. For example, there are some characters that can use fire shots as projectiles. Let's say you're using a character that shots thrice at a time, if you time it just right you will be able to do a 6 hit combo and I personally feel like this should be illegal as the opponent don't even get the chance to dodge or defend the projectiles. Imagine playing as Ryu and spamming fireballs endlessly and the opponent just loses the round if you time the fireballs correctly. I honestly have no clue if this is intentional or not in Verdict Guilty but still.

• Pausing game screen
-> This is more of a silly feature that could also be improved but it isn't that big of a deal after some hours of gameplay. The thing is that when you pause the game during a round by pressing "esc", you may accidentally press esc again with the intention to resume the game, and if you do press "esc" again, you will be taken back to the menu screen, causing you to lose all your progress. This happened to me a few times as I never press enter to resume a game, this might not happen to you but I think they could at least add another window that pops up when you press "esc" for the second time asking if you are sure that you really wanna go back to the menu. 

And finally, the game difficulty (which I do not consider to be an issue, cuz I haven't played the entire game and haven't messed with the game settings (I don't even know if there are settings that allows you to change the game difficulty) due to that, I am not considering this a complete issue, but I do feel like the game is just too easy overall, you can spam anything you want and YOU WIN the round regardless. there are no strategies to win a round. Pick any character you want and just press one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ button the entire game and you'll see how easy it is to win a game. But it's what I said, that's just my 1 hour experience and I don't know if you can spice up the game difficulty, and I'd apologize if I am mistaken.

Overall, Verdict Guilty is a good game for its price, If you get the chance to purchase it and you enjoy fighting games, just do it, keeping in mind that the game has a few negative points.

O game conta com uma arte gráfica sensacional, com destaque para a paleta de cores, que é um dos pontes fortes do título. Cada personagem possui seus próprios especiais e suas próprias armas, o que torna a experiência sempre diferente ao trocar de boneco. Existem diversos modos de jogo, tais como o modo história, versus, survival e practice, e mais alguns desbloqueáveis. Cada protagonista tem seu modo história próprio para  ser jogado, onde devemos vencer as lutas com os comandos pedidos. Possui conquistas relativamente fáceis, e como são poucas, é possível o platinar em pouco tempo. Ótimo para quem gosta. Tem um preço super acessível, além da vantagem de ser bem leve.
